sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Uruk: The First City
sources.note: Direct full essay read: southern Iraq, Uruk around 3200 BCE, clay-cone mosaics, administrative pictographs and Early Dynastic rival cities. Map warning comes from decoded local geometry.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Akkadian Period
sources.note: Indexed original full essay read, conquest of rival cities, independent cities after Akkadian fragmentation. Approximate chronology only.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Guide to the Collections: Ancient Near Eastern Art
sources.note: Indexed original printed pages 13 and 16 read; PDF opens but extracts no text. Query exact URL with "Ur-Nammu" or "Elamites" reproduces passages. Uses political sequence, business tablets, late Sumerian writing continuity; dated older framing and ethnic stereotypes not adopted.

sources.title: Richard L. Zettler, From Beneath the Temple
sources.note: Indexed primary excavation discussion identifies Third Dynasty of Ur as 2112 to 2004 BCE; conventional approximate chronology used in period boundaries.

sources.title: Electronic Text Corpus of Sumerian Royal Inscriptions, Ur-Namma 28
sources.note: Direct tool access failed; exact indexed original full composite text read. Query site.oracc.museum.upenn.edu/etcsri/Q000952 "Ur-Namma". RIME3/2.01.01.28, seven cone witnesses, UrIII/Girsu. Column i lines6,10 to18 gives title, boundary canal and checking route. Transliterated Sumerian sample; superscript determinative rendered as Unicode superscript ki, no invented glyph sequence.

sources.title: British Museum, Cuneiform tablet recording barley rations
sources.note: Museum-authored Google Arts and Culture record for BM1906,0512.2, original indexed full record read; BM direct object page failed. Uruinimgina regnal context, Bau temple Girsu, approximately200 workmen and children, ration quantities and Shasha. Do not equate sila with exact modern pints.

sources.title: Penn Today, At a southern Iraq site, unearthing the archaeological passing of time
sources.note: Direct original project interview read, tavern around2700BCE, benches, oven, food vessels and clay cooling installation. Tavern/public eatery is excavators’ interpretation.

sources.title: William B. Hafford, Mesopotamian City Life
sources.note: Direct full article read. Uses Education and Industry, Commerce and Work and Play only. Does NOT adopt erroneous Enanatuma/Enheduanna passage or mistaken gameboard square counts. Textile numbers and hypothetical baby-rattle scene omitted.

sources.title: Penn Museum, Ur-Nammu brick B16461
sources.note: Direct catalogue and indexed full record: Ur, UrIII, ca2112 to2095BCE, dog footprint, stamped temple and city-wall inscription.

sources.title: William B. Hafford, City of the Moon
sources.note: Direct full archaeological report read: Old Babylonian areaAH circa1900BCE, more than50 houses, courtyard seals Gimil-Ningizzida and Ningal-lamazi, vaulted underfloor burial and reused UrIII bricks. Later occupation clearly labelled.

sources.title: Steve Tinney, Texts, Tablets, and Teaching
sources.note: Direct full article read: Old Babylonian Nippur and Ur, elementary wedges, TypeII teacher/example and repeatedly erased student side, private houses and recyclable tablets. Schooldays literary satire not used as literal daily schedule.

sources.title: Penn Museum, Medical Tablet CBS14221
sources.note: Direct catalogue and indexed full record read: Nippur, Sumerian prescriptions, ca2200BCE DateMade field. Catalog period EarlyDynasticIIIB conflicts with date and historical register alternatives OldAkk/UrIII; public uses broad late-third-millennium and notes uncertain dating in evidence. No remedy contents invented.

sources.title: Anne-Elizabeth Dunn-Vaturi, Board Games from Ancient Egypt and the Near East
sources.note: Direct essay: TwentySquares from Ur royal graves around2600BCE, later Egypt transmission. No claim modern rule reconstruction is original Sumerian rulebook.

sources.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Statue of Gudea 59.2
sources.note: Direct catalogue read: diorite, clasped hands, probableGirsu and translated robe inscription. Dates differ within record (ca2090object and older2150to2125reign): public uses late-third-millennium only, no false exactpoint.

proposedOverrides.name: Sumer
proposedOverrides.summary: Southern Mesopotamia’s rival cities developed urban institutions, crafts and writing, whose influence outlasted successive kingdoms.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Exact existing indexed entity Sumer, alias Sumerian city-states. No runtime override/card or staged bundle found on claim scan. Broad regional history, not replacement for separate Akkadian or UrIII identities.
batchIdentityNotes.geometry: Decoded polygons at4000/3000/2000BCE remain around35.6084to43.2940E and33.4344to37.8516N, displaced northwest and excluding Ur/Uruk in southern Iraq. Public opening explicitly identifies invalid heartland representation. No geometry correction claimed. Full evidence ../identity-all-snapshots.json.
batchIdentityNotes.dates: Imported4000to1500BCE cultural interval retained as map_coverage. Periods approximate. ThirdDynastyUr conventional2112to2004BCE. OldBabylonian households and school explicitly later phase, not timelessSumerian customs. Existing base fell2334 field overridden null because one conquest cannot represent this broad region’s end.
